accessibility: The button is named "Workbench preferences"; each row is a checkbox item whose checked state is announced, the check is never the only sign of the choice.
The menu is reachable and operable by keyboard: arrows move, Space or Enter chooses.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Button, Divider, Menu, MenuLabel, MenuItem); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The menu is a Menu under its button, drawn open; a check item shows its choice, which a Variant sets, and the choice itself is not interactive. The tooltip of the button and the closing on an outside press are not modelled.
The app repeats each group's hint (its menu shows the description twice, and the language hint is clipped at the menu edge); the hint is modelled once, as designed.
The names of the languages are identities and keep their own script: English and 繁體中文.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n; en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets, the strings of the app copied under the same Locale keys.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A member pressed the preferences button of the top bar; the menu opens under it, aligned to the end, 288px wide.
The base state follows the system for both the theme and the language, with single-key shortcuts on: the member never chose anything.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the menu is Workbench chrome, so its text follows the Workbench language and is baked here per Locale.
spec.intent: Show the Workbench preferences menu, opened from the sliders button at the end of the top bar, as built from Adapter Widgets only: the theme and the language of the Workbench chrome, each a choice of following the system or fixing one value, then the single-key shortcuts switch and the entry that opens the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
interactionRules: Each of the two groups shows its choice with a check at the end of the row; choosing a row applies it at once and keeps the menu open, so the next preference can be changed in the same visit.
Match system returns the language to the browser's; any other choice is kept for this browser until Match system is chosen again.
Both groups say, under their title, that they change the Workbench only: the previewed View keeps its own Locale and theme, which are chosen in the render context bar of the canvas.
Single-key shortcuts is a switch with a check while on; with it off, only the shortcuts that hold a modifier key work. Keyboard shortcuts opens the dialog that lists them.
